subject: Architecture
title: Light Pollution: Erasing the Stars
description: A 60-second lesson on Light Pollution: Erasing the Stars.

hook.text: 80% of Americans can no longer see the Milky Way from where they live. Buildings and streetlights erased it.

buildup.text: Upward-facing lights on buildings scatter off atmosphere particles — creating a dome of artificial glow over cities.

discovery.text: Light pollution disrupts animal behavior — sea turtles follow city lights instead of moonlit oceans.

twist.text: Blue-white LED streetlights are worse than old sodium lights — they scatter more broadly across the sky.

climax.text: Dark sky preserves and shielded lighting designs are slowly bringing stars back to the edges of cities.

punchline.text: We lit up our cities and blacked out the universe.

quiz.question: Why are LED streetlights worse for light pollution than older sodium lights?
options: They use more electricity and stay on longer
Blue-white light scatters more broadly across the sky
They are mounted higher on taller poles
